claims.text: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles contain inherent or simulated local compositional fluctuations.
Local compositional inhomogeneities govern the onset and progression of melting in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Cu-enriched regions act as nucleation sites for melting.
Cu enrichment lowers the local melting temperature.
Cu-rich regions have a lower melting point than regions dominated by the other alloy components.
Cu-rich or low-cohesive-energy regions reduce the local activation barrier for melting.
The liquid phase nucleates preferentially in Cu-rich or low-cohesive-energy regions.
Increasing temperature accelerates atomic diffusion and thereby propagates melting away from the initial nucleation regions.
Melting proceeds heterogeneously, beginning in compositionally weakened regions and spreading through the nanoparticle.
Nanoparticles with pronounced compositional inhomogeneity will begin melting at a lower temperature than compositionally uniform nanoparticles.
Nanoparticles with pronounced compositional inhomogeneity will exhibit a more spatially heterogeneous phase transformation than compositionally uniform nanoparticles.
Artificially homogenized nanoparticles will initiate melting more uniformly.
Artificially homogenized nanoparticles will initiate melting at a relatively higher temperature.
The proposed mechanism applies in the premelting-to-melting regime, where thermal activation can overcome local bonding differences.
The melting-onset shift depends on the magnitude of the local compositional deviation.
